description:
You are a site reliability engineer tasked with monitoring server uptime by analyzing raw ping logs. In the directory /home/user/uptime_logs, there is a file named ping_results.txt. Each line in this file consists of a single timestamp in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format, followed by a space, and then the word "UP" or "DOWN" (indicating whether the server responded to the ping). Example lines:

2024-06-11 14:00:00 UP  
2024-06-11 14:01:00 DOWN  

Your goal is to determine, for all logs in ping_results.txt, how many times the server was reported as "UP" and how many times as "DOWN". Count the occurrences for each status, then save the result in the file /home/user/uptime_logs/status_frequency.txt.

The output in status_frequency.txt must have the following format (exact spacing required):

UP <tab> <number_of_occurrences_of_UP>  
DOWN <tab> <number_of_occurrences_of_DOWN>  

For example, if there were 123 occurrences of UP and 7 occurrences of DOWN, the output file should contain:

UP    123  
DOWN    7  

Do not include any blank lines in the output file. Tab characters, not spaces, must separate the status word and the count. After you create the output file, display its contents in the terminal.
truth:
Directory /home/user/uptime_logs/ exists before the task begins.  
File /home/user/uptime_logs/ping_results.txt exists and contains the following lines:

2024-06-11 10:00:00 UP
2024-06-11 10:01:00 UP
2024-06-11 10:02:00 UP
2024-06-11 10:03:00 DOWN
2024-06-11 10:04:00 UP
2024-06-11 10:05:00 DOWN
2024-06-11 10:06:00 UP
2024-06-11 10:07:00 UP
2024-06-11 10:08:00 UP
2024-06-11 10:09:00 UP

The agent must produce the file /home/user/uptime_logs/status_frequency.txt with exactly this content (using tab characters for spacing):

UP<TAB>8
DOWN<TAB>2

(where <TAB> is the ASCII 0x09 character, not literal spaces).  
The agent must display the content of /home/user/uptime_logs/status_frequency.txt to the terminal.  
No blank lines in the output file.
